title: A visual path for learning with AI
message: 10 November 2026 · Mykolas Romeris University · 12:30–14:10 · Room III-326

cards.title: Who is it for?
cards.body: University students and teachers. Make initial knowledge and decisions about learning visible.

cards.title: What will we do?
cards.body: Set a goal, map what we know, plan next steps and check AI suggestions against reliable sources. Use concept maps, reflection and self-assessment.

cards.title: What will you take away?
cards.body: A reusable activity template and practical tasks for autonomy, critical thinking, uncertainty and managing frustration.

takeaway: Prepared examples and worksheets allow participation without a personal AI account.

title: Andrea needs to understand GenAI
message: One student’s learning process, from assignment to assessment
body: Andrea is a second-year computer science student: he can program, but still confuses key concepts of generative models.
He must study a chapter and explain how a language model generates text.
We observe his use of tools and the evidence of understanding he keeps.
decision: You are following the learning method; you do not need to learn programming.

character.happyAlt: Andrea smiles confidently, with empty hands resting together at his waist.
character.worriedAlt: Andrea looks worried as he struggles to support an enormous, very thick textbook with both hands. Its cover reads Foundations of Generative Artificial Intelligence, by Marco Cremaschi.

title: Andrea’s learning task
message: To understand the chapter and show what he has learned, Andrea must:

steps.title: Read
steps.text: Study the chapter. Identify the key ideas and what is still unclear.

steps.title: Represent
steps.text: Build a diagram with labelled links between the concepts.

steps.title: Check
steps.text: Compare the diagram and AI suggestions with the chapter. Correct errors.

steps.title: Explain
steps.text: Use his own words to explain a new example, without AI help.

decision: Evidence: a checked diagram, an independent explanation and a justified correction.

title: Self-directed learning: making choices
message: Andrea takes an active role: he identifies his learning needs, chooses a path and reviews his progress.

comparison.label: 1. Identify a goal
comparison.text: What do I need to learn, and what do I want to achieve?

comparison.label: 2. Choose a path
comparison.text: Which resources, people and strategies will help me learn?

comparison.label: 3. Review progress
comparison.text: What can I explain now, and what needs more work? Self-assessment helps here.

result: “I need to distinguish training from inference. I will use the chapter and a concept map, then check whether I can explain the difference.”
decision: Andrea takes responsibility for his choices, with support from teachers and peers.

title: Self-assessment: checking progress
message: Andrea judges his progress against clear criteria, then uses that judgement to improve his work.

comparison.label: 1. Check the criteria
comparison.text: What should I be able to explain or do?

comparison.label: 2. Look for evidence
comparison.text: What can I demonstrate? Where do I still struggle?

comparison.label: 3. Choose a next step
comparison.text: What will I revise, practise or check again?

result: “I can explain the main ideas, but I still struggle to show how they connect. I will revise my map and explain those connections again.”
decision: AI can offer feedback; the learner checks the evidence and decides what to improve.

title: A study process in six phases

steps.title: PLAN
steps.text: Set your goal, identify your starting point and organise tasks and time.

steps.title: UNDERSTAND
steps.text: Clarify difficult ideas through explanations, examples and questions.

steps.title: CONNECT
steps.text: Explain ideas in your own words and organise relationships between concepts.

steps.title: RECALL
steps.text: Retrieve what you know without looking, then revisit it over time.

steps.title: APPLY
steps.text: Use what you have learned to solve problems and handle new situations.

steps.title: CHECK
steps.text: Compare your performance with criteria, identify gaps and decide what to study next.

decision: Checking guides your next step. SUPPORT marks setup, sources and sharing.

title: Agent Skills: reusable workflows
message: A skill gives an agent a reusable method for a specific task.

comparison.label: Instructions
comparison.text: SKILL.md describes when to use the skill and the steps the agent should follow.

comparison.label: Resources
comparison.text: References, examples and templates provide context and guide the output.

comparison.label: Optional scripts
comparison.text: Bundled code can carry out specific operations as part of the workflow.

decision: When a task calls for it, the agent reads SKILL.md and loads supporting files as needed.

title: Where skills can run
message: Check the product and the runtime before choosing a skill.

comparison.label: ChatGPT
comparison.text: Recorded here in ChatGPT web: Plugins → Skills → upload a package, then select it in Work mode. Availability depends on the account and workspace.

comparison.label: Coding agents
comparison.text: Codex and other compatible agents can load skill packages. Scripts may require Python, Node or network access.

decision: A shared file format does not guarantee identical tools, installation or results.
